caption: The drawing contains three rectangular wooden sample illustrations arranged in two rows: two on the top row and one on the bottom left. Each rectangle depicts a piece of wood with visible grain patterns. The top left rectangle is labeled “WARM SEPIA NO. 1” and is light brown with subtle grain lines in a darker sepia tone. The top right rectangle is labeled “WASH OF RAW SIENNA NO. 2” and is a similar size but has a slightly yellower hue, with less pronounced but still visible grain lines. The rectangle at the bottom left is labeled “WARM SEPIA - RAW SIENNA - IVORY BLACK Age with ivory black or umber stipple with ivory black NO. 3” and shows a wood piece with a combination of deeper brown and black tones, suggesting a more aged appearance, with varied and slightly darker grain patterns. To the right of the bottom rectangle is handwritten text explaining that the grain shown is about the actual size of wood and should be reduced in proportion for drawings; the bottom right corner has the name “HARRY MANN WADDELL.” The background of the drawing is a plain off-white.
title: Technique Demo (Wood Grain)
